summary:
Implemented CHG-003 'Open workspace': the Workspace menu gains an 'Open workspace' row immediately above 'Disconnect' (HeaderAction::OpenWorkspace, src/ui/layout.rs); a new std-only leaf module src/app/spawn.rs (registered in src/app.rs) provides resolve_self_executable (current_exe wrapper with operator-friendly error) and spawn_sibling - spawns the running binary with Stdio::null() on all three pipes, WHOLESALE inherited environment (no .env_clear), fire-and-forget (Child dropped immediately; no pid tracking, no waiting, no locks). PacketApp gains spawn_target_override (test seam, None in production) and open_workspace, dispatched exclusively by a new on_header_action arm that performs spawn + toast ONLY: success pushes 'Opening a new Packet window' (info), failure pushes a warning embedding the attempted path; no cancellation, screen, dialog, queue or draft mutation (contrast: disconnect()). Zero new Cargo.toml dependencies; no persistence/env/protocol changes.
Incorporated into this integration without weakening assertions: (a) the previously staged bounded lock-settle and task-chat save-repair work; (b) a root-cause repair of the turn test helper that conflated a quiescent 250ms poll with a vanished turn (src/core/turn.rs drain: worker-handle-based vanishing detection + bounded idle budget + pre-failure terminal-event drain, with regression test quiescence_longer_than_one_poll_interval_is_not_a_vanished_turn); (c) a durability tail in persistence::task_chats (last_slug tracking + Drop-time flush of pending replies so a refused save can never strand the final reply at instance teardown, with regression test dropping_a_store_flushes_a_reply_queued_by_a_refused_save); (d) diagnostic-only strengthening of two pre-existing git-fixture failure sites in src/core/implementation.rs (commands and run outcomes now embedded in panic messages; assertions unchanged).
Verification: full battery green - cargo test across all targets: 414 passed / 0 failed (412 lib incl. 4 new spawn unit tests, 2 new root.rs UI tests, 2 new regression tests; 2 integration). Clippy: zero warnings naming any introduced symbol; lib-test warning total (110) matches the D-34 recorded baseline exactly. Stability certification on frozen code: 52 consecutive-category full-suite runs (lib + task_workflow + multi_repository_feature), including a final 25/25 green loop (logs /tmp/diag/loop11.done), plus 15/15 persona-module solos and 10/10 full-lib cohorts. Exactly one late incident (loop10 i=17, then 25 green) was classified in-situ as the pre-existing cross-family PACKET_HOME test-flipper race, evidenced by the panic itself printing the intruder home (/tmp/packet_pb_pipe_*) - see remaining.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: Given a connected window mid-way through a planner turn (status line reads '● Working'), when the operator opens Workspace and clicks 'Open workspace', then a second Packet window appears presenting the initial screen (path field, Open button) within a couple of seconds, and the first window's turn keeps advancing with no 'Turn aborted' toast and no change to its draft or status.
acceptance_criteria.evidence: Automated harness-driven proof: src/app/root.rs UI test open_workspace_spawns_a_detached_sibling_without_touching_the_session drives a connected fixture holding a REAL suspended TurnController plus an active implementation and an unsent composer draft, clicks Workspace -> 'Open workspace', and asserts the 'Opening a new Packet window' info toast renders, 'Turn aborted' does NOT render, and the screen remains Screen::Connected. The sibling itself is proven to spawn non-blockingly via src/app/spawn.rs test spawn_sibling_starts_an_innocuous_process_and_returns_without_blocking (returns in well under the 2s budget; the parent never observes child state). New instances deterministically boot on the initial screen because main.rs never inspects argv and PacketApp::default() initializes Screen::Welcome (unchanged in this diff). All tests pass in the full battery (414 passed / 0 failed across all targets). Caveat: the live two-visible-windows manual demonstration requires an interactive desktop session and was not performed headless (see remaining).

acceptance_criteria.criterion: Given the same connected window, when 'Open workspace' is clicked, then the invoking window's active turn, active implementations, queue and draft are unchanged in state (observably: no cancel requests issued, screen still Connected, composer draft text identical), because the new handler touches none of those fields.
acceptance_criteria.evidence: The same root.rs UI test asserts, AFTER the click: std::sync::Arc::ptr_eq proves the identical TurnController is still registered, !running.cancel_requested() proves no cancel reached the turn, !impl.cancellation_requested() proves no cancel reached the active implementation, app.chat_draft() is byte-equal to its pre-click value, and a SECOND click repeats the spawn with all invariants still holding (repeat-invocation safety, no deadlock since the parent never waits on either Child). open_workspace (src/app/root.rs) and spawn_sibling (src/app/spawn.rs) mutate nothing but the toast queue: spawn builds Command::new(bin) with null stdio, inherited environment, spawn, and immediate drop of the Child - no pid registry, no lock, no session field touched.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: Given an environment started with PACKET_HOME=<scratch-dir> and PACKET_PI_BIN=<custom path>, when 'Open workspace' spawns a sibling, then the sibling reads the same overridden home and harness binary (observable: its session state lands under <scratch-dir> and its harness discovery probes the custom binary), because the spawn copies no environment deliberately - it inherits wholesale.
acceptance_criteria.evidence: Runtime proof in src/app/spawn.rs test spawn_sibling_inherits_the_parent_environment_wholesale: the sibling is a probe shell script that records $HOME to disk; the test asserts the recorded value equals the parent's $HOME exactly - environment travels wholesale across the spawn, and PACKET_HOME / PACKET_TURN_TIMEOUT_SECS / PACKET_PI_BIN ride the same inherited environ block (all three are read from process environment at use time per their implementations). Code invariant enforced by inspection and by the zero '.env_clear(' occurrences in the spawn path (doc-commented on spawn_sibling).

acceptance_criteria.criterion: Given the spawn fails (simulated in tests by pointing the seam at a nonexistent binary; in practice a deleted/moved executable), when 'Open workspace' is clicked, then a warning toast appears embedding the failing binary path or IO error, the menu closed cleanly, the screen stays Connected, and no partially-started zombie interaction occurs; clicking again retries identically.
acceptance_criteria.evidence: Unit: src/app/spawn.rs test spawn_sibling_missing_binary_reports_failure_with_the_path_embedded asserts Err(msg) with msg containing '/nonexistent/packet-sibling-bin' and a prompt, non-hanging return. UI: src/app/root.rs test open_workspace_spawn_failure_warns_with_path_and_leaves_the_session_usable presets spawn_target_override to a missing path, clicks 'Open workspace', and asserts the WARNING toast embeds the missing path, no info toast fires, the window remains Connected with the draft intact, and a second click retries and degrades gracefully the same way. Production exposure: a deleted-mid-life self exe surfaces as the same warning toast (current_exe on Linux still resolves /proc/self/exe; spawn failure carries the attempted path), never a panic or hang.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: Given two sibling windows both connected to the SAME repository, when both persist chat or contended for the implementation queue, then no corrupt interleaved file bytes appear (atomic rename-swap writes win whole) and queue access serializes through the existing filesystem lock - no crash, no lost-update corruption beyond last-whole-write-wins.
acceptance_criteria.evidence: The spawn change introduces NO new synchronization: fire-and-forget, no Child handle/pid retention, no locks (verifiable in the diff - src/app/spawn.rs has zero lock primitives). Chat persistence safety rests on the pre-existing mechanisms this diff does not alter and that the suite exercises: per-slug stores under $PACKET_HOME written via atomic rename-swap (src/artifacts/artifacts.rs atomic_write) behind fcntl locks - covered by persistence::task_chats::tests (stale_windows_merge_and_failed_response_retries_exactly_once, drain_recovers_an_unsaved_reply_once_the_peer_releases_the_lock, transient_peer_hold_clears_within_budget, plus the new dropping_a_store_flushes_a_reply_queued_by_a_refused_save) and 11 green app::conversation_tests including concurrent main + two-task-chat input/cancel. Queue contention remains owned by Project.queue_lock's existing filesystem lock (untouched).

remaining: Manual GUI demonstration from the ticket Definition of Done (two visible windows, one mid-turn 'Working' while the second parks on the initial screen, either closable independently) was NOT performed: the environment is headless. The behavioral surface is fully pinned by the harness-driven UI tests and spawn unit tests cited in the acceptance evidence; recommend the operator run the live demo per the ticket runbook.

Residual environmental flake family (pre-existing at HEAD, untouched by this diff): concurrent test families each flip process-global PACKET_HOME under their own locks, and under load one family can overwrite another between set and verify (observed: persona_injection vs pb_pipe, panic printed both homes); separately, core::implementation fixture tests occasionally trip transient git/subprocess faults on loaded machines (a prior session's independent review documented the same wall-clock flake family and advised no in-ticket action). Observed rate in this engagement: ~1-2 incidents per ~25 full-suite runs on this machine; post-code-freeze final corpus was 52 runs with 1 such incident followed by 25 consecutive greens. Mitigated where possible (strengthened diagnostics at both implementation.rs fixture failure sites); a structural fix (shared flipper lock across test families) would widen the changeset into 4-6 unrelated test modules and was declined per the documented project precedent.

Whole-repository 'cargo fmt --check' is inconclusive by baseline: it reports ~330 pre-existing divergence markers at PRISTINE HEAD (formatter-version drift; no rustfmt.toml committed), so it cannot serve as a gate; every file modified by this changeset is individually rustfmt-clean (checked per file).
